problem_statement: Ideas currently go straight from a human's head into implementation with no structured requirements-gathering step in between. There is no reusable mechanism for interviewing a human, drafting a complete requirements spec, having it critiqued for gaps/contradictions, and producing a versioned artifact that a downstream architect persona can act on without needing to go back to the human for basic clarifications.
purpose_and_goals: Build a reusable 'PM persona' loop: a conversational requirements-gathering flow that (1) detects whether it was given a raw idea or an existing artifact to refine, (2) interviews the human to fill a required checklist of spec fields, (3) drafts a structured spec, (4) has a distinct critic persona review the draft for consistency/completeness/testability, (5) routes critic findings back to the PM for targeted follow-up questions (not just handed to the human), (6) gets explicit human sign-off, and (7) writes a versioned project_spec.json that a separate architect persona can build from without further clarifying questions.

target_users.primary: The repo owner (Jared), for personal/side projects
target_users.design_intent: Built for personal use first, but intentionally generic/reusable — not hardcoded to any single project's domain or vocabulary, so other developers/teams could adopt it

supported_inputs: A rough, unstructured one-line idea with near-zero existing context
An existing artifact (issue, doc, ticket, partial spec) that needs gaps filled and tightening
trigger_and_input_handling.behavior: Persona auto-detects which case it's in and adapts its interview accordingly (starting from scratch vs. targeted gap-filling)

interview_behavior.pacing: One question at a time by default; may batch 2-3 short, clearly independent questions (e.g. simple yes/no fields) but never bundles questions whose answers depend on each other
interview_behavior.handling_uncertain_answers: If the human gives a vague, contradictory, or 'I don't know' answer, the persona does not just record it or silently drop it — it offers clarifying context, examples, or a tradeoff/impact explanation to help the human answer meaningfully before moving on
interview_behavior.priority_and_estimates: Persona infers a priority ranking (must-have vs. later/nice-to-have) and rough timeline/cost sizing from the conversation, then explicitly presents that inference back to the human for confirmation or correction — it never invents these from nothing, and never skips asking the human to confirm

stop_condition.primary: Persona tracks a checklist of required spec fields and drives toward full coverage (each field answered or explicitly marked N/A)
stop_condition.override: The human can say 'that's enough' / 'generate the spec' at any point; persona will draft from whatever's been gathered so far and explicitly flags the resulting gaps rather than pretending they don't exist

required_spec_fields_checklist: integration_context (where/how it will run, what it integrates with, any constraints the human already knows about)

security_and_risk_considerations (data sensitivity, secrets/credentials handling, threat/abuse considerations, what distinct access levels/roles are needed in plain terms, whether infrastructure should be defined as code)
regulatory_and_compliance_constraints (data residency requirements, PII/sensitive-data handling rules, any applicable compliance regimes the human is aware of, e.g. GDPR/HIPAA)
supply_chain_security_expectations (whether dependency scanning, artifact signing, or vulnerability management are expected/required for this project)
cost_sensitivity (whether compute/token cost is a hard constraint for this project or a non-issue, as stated by the human)
open_questions_for_architect (anything left unresolved or explicitly deferred)
revision_history (critic findings per round + how each was resolved)

draft_and_review_loop.roles: Two distinct personas/perspectives: the PM (drafts, interviews) and a separate Critic (adversarial review — looking specifically for gaps, contradictions, untestable acceptance criteria) — not the same persona self-reviewing its own work
critic_checks: completeness against the required fields checklist
security/risk considerations were explicitly addressed, not left blank — a spec cannot pass review with this field empty or skipped
regulatory/compliance, supply chain security, and cost sensitivity fields were explicitly addressed (answered or explicitly marked N/A), not silently left blank
draft_and_review_loop.on_findings: Critic findings route back to the PM persona, which asks the human targeted follow-up questions to resolve just the flagged issues, then re-drafts — the critic does not present findings directly to the human itself
draft_and_review_loop.cycle_cap: Hard cap of 4 PM<->critic revision cycles, with a target of resolving within 2-3; if the cap is hit, escalate to the human directly rather than looping further
draft_and_review_loop.final_step: After the critic is satisfied, the human must give explicit sign-off before the spec is considered final

output_handling.location: Path is provided by whoever invokes the loop (e.g. ./docs/project_spec.json for this session) — persona writes there
output_handling.versioning: Prior versions are preserved, not overwritten, when the persona is re-invoked to amend an existing spec (exact file-naming/versioning mechanism left to the architect persona to design)
output_handling.audit_trail: Final spec retains a revision_history section documenting what the critic flagged each round and how it was resolved, not just the clean final answer

resumability.note: If an interview session is interrupted, restarting from scratch is acceptable for v1

handoff_to_architect.mechanism_for_v1: Manual — the PM persona writes the final project_spec.json and stops; a human decides when/how to invoke the architect persona next. No automatic triggering in v1.
handoff_to_architect.future_direction: Other loop types beyond this initial spec-gathering+critic loop are expected to tie directly into this architecture handoff, but are not designed or scoped now

devsecops_requirements.spec_content_level: Every project spec the PM persona produces must include a security_and_risk_considerations field covering: data sensitivity, secrets/credentials handling, threat/abuse considerations, what distinct access levels/roles are needed in plain terms (e.g. admin vs. viewer, internal vs. external users), and whether the target project's infrastructure should be defined as code (IaC) — the PM records these as gathered requirements/preferences, it does not decide the IAM model (roles, policies, federation strategy) or IaC tooling itself. The critic must explicitly verify this field was addressed before approving the spec — not just check it exists as an empty field.
devsecops_requirements.pm_agent_loop_project_level: Applies to how pm-agent-loop itself is built/operated, not just spec content: no secrets/API keys ever logged, printed, or committed; dependency and static-security scanning in CI (repo already has ruff configured with bandit rules ('S') and Dependabot enabled — architect should build on/extend these rather than replace them, exact CI security gates left to the architect to design)

regulatory_supply_chain_and_finops_requi.rationale: The architect persona prompt (prompts/02_architecture_definition_prompt.md) produces dedicated Regulatory & Compliance, Supply Chain Security, and FinOps/Cost sections, and resolves ambiguity by asking the human directly one question at a time. Since a stated success criterion is that the architect shouldn't need to go back to the human for basics, the PM persona must gather these upfront rather than leaving them entirely to the architect's own interview.
regulatory_supply_chain_and_finops_requi.requirement: PM persona must ask the human about known regulatory/compliance constraints, supply chain security expectations, and cost sensitivity during the interview, recording whatever the human states (including 'none' or 'unsure') — the PM does not research compliance regimes or decide tooling itself, it only records stated requirements/preferences.

non_goals: Choosing architecture, frameworks, or tech stack — always deferred to the architect persona
Writing or editing any source code
success_criteria: Primary bar: the architect persona can take a produced project_spec.json and produce a build plan without needing to go back to the human for basic clarifications
Secondary signal: the human interview itself surfaces considerations they hadn't thought of, without feeling tedious or redundant

must_have_v1: Input-type detection (raw idea vs. existing artifact)
One-at-a-time (with limited trivial batching) checklist-driven interview, including tradeoff-based follow-up on vague answers
Draft -> distinct Critic review -> PM follow-up loop, capped at 4 cycles (target 2-3)
Versioned output file with critic revision-history audit trail

DevSecOps: security_and_risk_considerations required in every produced spec + critic gate enforcing it; pm-agent-loop's own build process avoids logging/committing secrets and uses dependency/static-security scanning (building on existing ruff bandit rules + Dependabot)
later_nice_to_have: Support for multiple distinct named loop types (e.g. new-feature spec, bug triage, architecture-change spec) with differently-shaped output
Automatic handoff/invocation of the architect persona loop
priority_ranking.sizing: v1 is a small-to-medium scoped effort: a single Python package, no external services required, confirmed by the user as directionally correct

open_questions_for_architect: Execution/consumption model is undecided: standalone Python CLI/library, a Claude Code skill/subagent, or both (core engine as a library with a thin CLI + Claude Code integration). User does not have a preference and defers this choice to the architect.
Exact versioning/file-naming scheme for preserved prior spec versions
Whether/how the Critic role is implemented as a genuinely distinct persona (e.g. separate prompt/system role) vs. same model with different framing

Schema/validation mechanism for project_spec.json (issue/PR templates in this repo hint at Pydantic models and an AgentState-style structure, but this is not confirmed as a decision, only a hint from existing repo scaffolding)
Specific CI security tooling to add beyond the existing ruff bandit ('S') rules and Dependabot (e.g. SAST/secret-scanning tools, SBOM generation) — left to the architect to select

Quality gates / Definition of Done are generated downstream by the sprint-breakdown persona from the Architecture Definition Document (per prompts/03_agile_sprint_breakdown_prompt.md), not gathered by the PM — architect/sprint-breakdown personas should derive these from testing/CI conventions and whatever tech stack is chosen, not expect them pre-supplied in project_spec.json
